summary: The study fabricated four Ti3C2Tx solid-state micro-supercapacitor electrodes differing in urea-space-holder loading and resulting film density/porosity: pristine 2.11 g/cm3 and porous films of 1.78, 1.44, and 1.15 g/cm3. MXene was prepared from Ti3AlC2 by LiF/HCl MILD etching and vortex delamination; porous coatings were made by urea removal followed by water/acetone solvent exchange. The 1.44 g/cm3, 72% porous electrode was the headline sample, delivering 192 F/g and 241 mF/cm2 at 5 mV/s in H2SO4-PVA gel electrolyte. Numerical capacitances were not printed for the 1.78 g/cm3 electrode, and dry thickness, mass loading, flake dimensions, and per-sample pore diameters were not reported.
